title: Don't be a meat proxy
blurb: The author argues that pasting an AI's verbatim output into Slack, code reviews, or group chats adds no value, since anyone can query the model themselves faster and with better context. Real contribution comes from reading, validating, and rewriting the response in your own words, which serves as proof you actually did the work rather than acting as a "meat proxy" between the reader and the model.

title: Don't be a meat proxy

Pasting a raw Claude response adds no value, since the recipient could query the model themselves with better context control. The real contribution is reading, understanding, and validating the output, then responding in your own words as evidence that you did that work.

title: The Agent Access Model
blurb: Cloudflare's paper proposes the Agent Access Model (AAM), an access framework for software agents that BeyondCorp-style Zero Trust does not cover because it assumes a human working at human speed. Rather than making each access decision smarter, AAM shrinks the agent's capability ceiling per task-scoped run so there is less to judge, addressing controls that fail quietly by granting too much and trusting for too long.

title: The Agent Access Model
blurb: Cloudflare proposed the Agent Access Model (AAM), an access-control framework for AI agents that argues human-shaped controls like SSO, device posture, and conditional access fail silently against software principals by granting too much, seeing too little, and trusting too long. Rather than making each access decision smarter, AAM shrinks the agent's capability ceiling per task-scoped run so there is less to authorize in the first place, and it separates single-principal controls available today from the unsolved problem of multiplayer access control.

title: Russia moves to restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether and USDT
blurb: Russia's central bank will restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether, and USDT on regulated exchanges starting September 1, capping non-qualified investors at 300,000 rubles (approx. $3,600) of purchases per intermediary annually while exempting qualified investors. The per-intermediary structure lets traders exceed that ceiling across multiple brokers, and crypto payments inside Russia remain prohibited under the July legislation these rules build on.
